copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Buries The League's Best Team
copies.body:
The running backs decided this one before anything else did. Chuba Hubbard went for 34.2, Jonathan Taylor added 12.3, and Ollie Gordon II kicked in 15.5 from the flex — CJ got 62 points out of three roster spots while Adam's backfield of Rico Dowdle and Kimani Vidal mustered 8.8 combined. That's a 37.7-point hole at running back alone, which is more than enough to eat a 12.2-point loss and a Steelers defense that posted negative seven.
Adam actually won four of seven positions. Brock Purdy's 31.7 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 31.1 were terrific. But Chris Olave missed by nearly ten, Sam LaPorta missed by nearly nine, and Jalen Coker's 0.3 in the flex was a tombstone with Antonio Williams and his 12.2 sitting on the bench. We picked Adam by 21; the flex spot alone was a 15-point swing the other way.
CJ's 5-5 now, luck +0.6, all-play still a middling 44 percent — he's stealing these, and he'll take it. Adam falls to 7-3 and remains the best team in the league by every metric that doesn't count wins.

copies.headline: Logan's flex and defense cost him again
copies.body:
The margin lived in two spots Logan barely thinks about. Germie Bernard put up 1.0 in the flex on a 10.9 projection, and the Chiefs defense managed 9.0 against Kaleb's Vikings and their 21.0. That's 22 points of gap right there — more than double the 9.7 final. Joe Burrow's 33.2 and Isaiah Likely's 27.7 built a 24-point lead at QB and TE, and Logan still lost, because Tetairoa McMillan (6.5 on 16.0) and Jaylen Warren (9.1 on 15.5) spent the afternoon subtracting it back.
Kaleb didn't do anything spectacular. Six starters between 10 and 17, Breece Hall and Drake London leading a committee, and the Vikings defense doing the heavy lifting. For a team scoring 103.2 a game, 127.4 is a party.
We had Logan by 17, which now looks optimistic. He's 4-6 with a 66-44 all-play and two wins fewer than he's earned — fourth in scoring, ninth in results. Kaleb is 6-4 at 36% all-play, which is less a team than a rumor.

copies.headline: Christian's Backfield Buries Noah's New England Problem
copies.body:
The game was over at the hinge positions. Christian got 48.6 from Chase Brown and Bhayshul Tuten while Noah's running backs managed 23.2, and the quarterback spot was worse: Trevor Lawrence 26.8, Drake Maye 3.0 — now listed out with an ankle — against a 22-point projection. That's 49 points of edge from two slots. Noah actually won wide receiver by 5.1 and flex by 8.1 and it didn't matter in the slightest.
Rhamondre Stevenson's 1.5 on a 13.4 projection was the other wound, and Seth McGowan sat on Noah's bench with 13.7. Christian had his own sins — Deebo Samuel scored 25.9 in street clothes while Khalil Shakir gave him 7.5 — but a 58.5-point win covers a lot. We had Christian by 18 and undersold it.
Christian's at 5-5 with a 70-40 all-play, third in scoring, and a minus-1.4 luck figure that says the record is a lie. Noah's 3-7 and 12th in all-play, which is where the postseason assassin usually starts his work.

copies.headline: McCaffrey Carries Leif Past Stalling John
copies.body:
The running backs settled this before anyone looked at a kicker. Christian McCaffrey went for 46.3 by himself, and Leif's backfield cleared John's 53.8 to 40.3 even with Woody Marks managing 7.5 on a 14.2 projection — he's now listed Out with a concussion. Add Josh Allen's 6.7-point edge over Drew Lock and Stefon Diggs doubling up John's entire receiver room, and the 19.2 margin was built three positions deep.
John's loss traces to two names. Kyren Williams gave him 5.2 against an 18.6 projection, and DeMario Douglas put up 1.4 while Xavier Hutchinson (15.8) and Malik Washington (13.4) sat on his bench. Either swap flips this game. That's the second straight loss for a team scoring 130.1 a week, second-best in the league, with an all-play of 70-40 to prove it isn't noise.
Leif is 7-3 on 115.3 a game and a 52-58 all-play — he's stealing these, and he knows it. We had him by nine. He took it by 19.

copies.headline: Gibbs And Dak Bury Isaac's Giants Problem
copies.body:
Mitchell won this in the backfield and under center, and it wasn't close. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 44.2 by himself — more than Isaac's entire running back room and flex combined — and Dak Prescott's 34.4 gave Mitchell a 14-point cushion at quarterback before anyone else touched the ball. Add DJ Moore's 19.4 in the flex against Wan'Dale Robinson's 4.0 and you've got the 18.7 margin three times over. Isaac actually won four positions. Didn't matter.
Isaac's problem was everything that wasn't Ja'Marr Chase (34.1) or Cam Skattebo (27.2). Malik Nabers missed projection by 8.7, Javonte Williams by 7.1, Robinson — now Questionable with an ankle — by 6.3. Ryan Flournoy's 19.1 sat on the bench watching. That alone flips the game.
Mitchell gets to 4-7 on his third straight week above 128, which is what -1.4 luck looks like finally correcting. We had him by seven; he beat it. Isaac drops to 5-5 and is still chasing 2022.

copies.headline: Mahomes And A Kicker Bury Peter
copies.body:
Grant won this at the two positions nobody drafts for. Patrick Mahomes put up 35.4 to Aaron Rodgers' 15.6, and Cam Little's 21.0 against Evan McPherson's 6.4 turned a close game into a 30.5-point burial. Add Tony Pollard's 23.9 and Amon-Ra St. Brown's 25.8 and Grant never needed his flex, which is good, because Christian Watson gave him 6.7 while Omarion Hampton (17.5) and Quinshon Judkins (16.1) rotted on the bench.
Peter got a monster from George Pickens — 43.5, more than Grant's entire wide receiver room — and still lost by five touchdowns' worth. The middle of his lineup collapsed: Brock Bowers 3.8 on a 15.4 projection and A.J. Brown 4.7 on 12.5, both now listed Out with ankle and hamstring issues respectively. Pat Freiermuth's 11.5 sitting behind Denzel Boston's 2.6 didn't help.
Three straight losses for the 2022 champ, now 5-5 with an all-play of 45-65 that says he should be worse. We had Grant by 13 and undersold it.

intro: Christian's 149.88 was the week's high-water mark and it landed on Noah, who managed 91.42 and never got out of the parking lot — a 58.5-point beating that doubles as a roster indictment. The closest call was Kaleb holding off Logan by 9.7 despite Logan posting a perfectly respectable 117.76, which is the kind of loss that ages badly. Elsewhere, Mitchell and Grant both cleared 148 to put away Isaac and Peter, so if you scored in the 110s this week, you mostly just picked the wrong opponent.
